_doc: Fact sheet for the scroll story. Every fact comes from the public record: the adopted Planning Commission motion (cited as 'motion p.N', N = page of the PDF) or the DataSF planning record for the case (read from the local snapshot of 2026-11-09). No private individual is named. Conditions are copied unchanged from tools/conditions-search/data/conditions.json.
address: 302 Greenwich Street / 1531 Montgomery Street, San Francisco, CA 94133

zoning.name: Residential, House - Three Family
also: Telegraph Hill - North Beach Residential Special Use District

what_was_asked: The applicant proposes to restore the abandoned Restaurant Use of City Landmark No. 121, Julius' Castle.

vote.text_as_printed:
AYES: Hillis, Richards, Fong, Melgar, Moore, Koppel, Johnson
NAYS: None
ABSENT: None
ADOPTED: July 6, 2017

notes: The PDF is a scan of the signed motion with a text layer; the pages are clear to read.
Page 15 carries conditions 17 to 22 (sidewalk, odour, liaison, roof terrace hours, entertainment, deliveries) and names no private person.
Page 1 prints the project sponsor's name and mailing address, and the staff planner's name, phone number and e-mail address. It is public, but the story should open on another page.
Page 2 names the architect of the 1920s building. Page 10 (the vote) carries the Commission Secretary's signature and names no private person.

sources.neighbourhood: motion p.2 ("Telegraph Hill/North Beach neighborhood"); the DataSF planning record says "North Beach"

timeline.event: Julius' Castle is built, and opens as a restaurant.
The restaurant closes and the building becomes vacant, after about 85 years.
A Certificate of Appropriateness case (2012.1197A) is opened. The planning record describes it: "To restore the historic operation of a landmark restaurant".
The Historic Preservation Commission approves the Certificate of Appropriateness for the exterior restoration (Motion No. 0213).
timeline.source: motion p.1 (date, body and motion number) and p.4 (exterior work)

timeline.event: The Planning Department approves an Administrative Certificate of Appropriateness that clarifies the scope of that work.
The project sponsor files for a rear yard variance, to legalize an expansion at the rear of the building that the motion says was built without a permit around 2007.
timeline.source: motion p.1 (filing) and p.4 (when the expansion was built)

timeline.event: The project sponsor files the Conditional Use application to bring the restaurant back.
The Planning Commission hears the case and adopts Motion No. 19958, 7 to 0, with 22 conditions.
The planning record for the case is closed as "Closed - Approved".
An appeal record (2016-001273APL) is opened under this case.
The appeal record is closed as "Closed - Appeal Denied".

story_facts.value: On the north side of Greenwich Street at the end of Montgomery Street, about 150 feet downslope from Coit Tower.

story_facts.fact: Why a restaurant is allowed in a residential district
story_facts.value: A use allowed on the ground floor of an NC-1 district may be approved in a designated landmark in an RH district, if it is essential to keeping the landmark (Planning Code Section 186.3).
Maximum occupancy of 152 people; about 115 guests at a time
30 to 35 employees over the course of the day
Mainly 5 pm to 10 pm daily, with a possible weekend brunch from 11 am to 2 pm
Two in support signed by 18 people in total; one in opposition representing 12 people
The Telegraph Hill Neighborhood Center stated its support.
More traffic and pedestrian safety, and noise and activity from the restaurant.

story_facts.fact: Other eating and drinking places within 300 feet

story_facts.value: Exempt from CEQA as a Class 3 categorical exemption

findings_highlights.quote: Operated as a restaurant from 1923 until becoming vacant in 2007, Julius' Castle was one of San Francisco's oldest continuously operated restaurants in its original location.

Per the landmark ordinance, the significance of the building lies in its architectural design and its role as a restaurant that serves as "a living slice from the history of the local Italian and restaurant communities."
Residents of the area have sent twenty-three letters in support of the proposal and eleven in opposition.
The concerns of opposing parties relate to increased traffic and related pedestrian safety issues, as well as noise and activity that may emanate from the Restaurant.
Within a 300-foot radius, there are no other eating and drinking uses, and no other commercial properties.
The Restaurant would operate from 5pm to 10pm, daily, and would have no service at the roof terrace after 9pm so as to minimize noise concerns.

conditions.title: Validity
conditions.text: Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period.

conditions.title: Expiration and Renewal
conditions.text: Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization.

conditions.title: Diligent pursuit
conditions.text: Diligent pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved.

conditions.title: Extension
conditions.text: Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay.

conditions.title: Conformity with Current Law
conditions.text: Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval.

conditions.title: Additional Project Authorization
conditions.text: Additional Project Authorization: The Project Sponsor must obtain/maintain approvals for a Rear Yard Variance and Certificate of Appropriateness to allow legalization of an expansion at the rear of the structure and to allow for exterior restoration work, respectively, and satisfy all the conditions thereof. The conditions set forth below are additional conditions required in connection with the Project.

conditions.title: Final Materials
conditions.text: Final Materials: T'he Project Sponsor shall continue to work with Planning Department on any building design. Final materials, glazing, color, texture, landscaping, and detailing shall be subject to Department staff review and approval. The architectural addenda shall be reviewed and approved by the Planning Department prior to issuance.
conditions.text_display: Final Materials: The Project Sponsor shall continue to work with Planning Department on any building design. Final materials, glazing, color, texture, landscaping, and detailing shall be subject to Department staff review and approval. The architectural addenda shall be reviewed and approved by the Planning Department prior to issuance.

conditions.title: Garbage, composting and recycling storage
conditions.text: Garbage, composting and recycling storage: Space for the collection and storage of garbage, composting, and recycling shall be provided within enclosed areas on the property and clearly labeled and illustrated on the building permit plans. Space for the collection and storage of recyclable and compostable materials that meets the size, location, accessibility and other standards specified by the San Francisco Recycling Program shall be provided at the ground level of the buildings.

conditions.title: Rooftop Mechanical Equipment
conditions.text: Rooftop Mechanical Equipment: Pursuant to Planning Code 141, the Project Sponsor shall submit a roof plan to the Planning Department prior to Planning approval of the building permit application. Rooftop mechanical equipment, if any is proposed as part of the Project, is required to be screened so as not to be visible from any point at or below the roof level of the subject building.

conditions.title: Odor Control Unit
conditions.text: Odor Control Unit: In order to ensure any significant noxious or offensive odors are prevented from escaping the premises once the project is operational, the building permit application to implement the project shall include air cleaning or odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the plans. Odor control ducting shall not be applied to the primary facade of the building.

conditions.title: Traffic and Parking
conditions.text: Traffic and Parking: The owner and owner's lessee shall be required to submit an operations plan to the Planning Department prior to the Departments approval of the first Site or Building Permit. Said plan shall include details on the following operational aspects of the Restaurant: 1) valet parking; 2) employee parking; and 3) customer access to the Restaurant (vehicular, public transit, etc.).

conditions.title: Bicycle Parking
conditions.text: Bicycle Parking: Pursuant to Planning Code Sections 155.1 and 155.4, the Project shall provide no fewer than 6 (six) Class 2 bicycle parking spaces. SFMTA has final authority on the type, placement and number of Class 2 bicycle racks within the public ROW. Prior to issuance of first architectural addenda, the project sponsor shall contact the SFMTA Bike Parking Program at bikeparking@sfmta.com to coordinate the installation of on-street bicycle racks and ensure that the proposed bicycle racks meet the SFMTA’s bicycle parking guidelines.

conditions.title: Enforcement
conditions.text: Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. T'he Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction.
conditions.text_display: Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction.

conditions.title: Revocation due to Violation of Conditions
conditions.text: Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization.

conditions.title: Commission Hearing and Written Performance Update
conditions.text: Commission Hearing and Written Performance Update: T'he Planning Commission shall hold a follow-up hearing to evaluate the operation of the business and adherence to the Conditions of Approval six (6) months from the date the property begins operation as a Restaurant. A written performance update shall be provided to the Planning Commission prior to this hearing and should include any recorded complaints with the San Francisco Police Department and any other general feedback from neighbors regarding operation of the Restaurant.
conditions.text_display: Commission Hearing and Written Performance Update: The Planning Commission shall hold a follow-up hearing to evaluate the operation of the business and adherence to the Conditions of Approval six (6) months from the date the property begins operation as a Restaurant. A written performance update shall be provided to the Planning Commission prior to this hearing and should include any recorded complaints with the San Francisco Police Department and any other general feedback from neighbors regarding operation of the Restaurant.

conditions.title: Garbage, Recycling, and Composting Receptacles
conditions.text: Garbage, Recycling, and Composting Receptacles: Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. Garbage shall be picked-up no earlier than 6:30 AM.

conditions.title: Sidewalk Maintenance
conditions.text: Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards.

conditions.title: Odor Control
conditions.text: Odor Control: While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises.

conditions.title: Community Liaison
conditions.text: Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. T'he Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. Should the contact information change, the Zoning Administrator shall be made aware of such change.
conditions.text_display: Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. Should the contact information change, the Zoning Administrator shall be made aware of such change.

conditions.title: Hours of Operation
conditions.text: Hours of Operation: T'he subject establishment is limited to principally-permitted hours of operation allowed in the NC-1 District, with the following additional limitations: the roof terrace shall be closed by 9:00 pm, daily.
conditions.text_display: Hours of Operation: The subject establishment is limited to principally-permitted hours of operation allowed in the NC-1 District, with the following additional limitations: the roof terrace shall be closed by 9:00 pm, daily.

conditions.title: Amplified, Live Entertainment
conditions.text: Amplified, Live Entertainment: 'The Restaurant shall not permit any amplified, live entertainment.
conditions.text_display: Amplified, Live Entertainment: The Restaurant shall not permit any amplified, live entertainment.

conditions.title: Delivery Hours
conditions.text: Delivery Hours: Deliveries to the property shall only occur between the hours of 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM.

condition_groups.label: hours
condition_groups.note: Roof terrace closing time and delivery hours. Condition 16 also sets an earliest garbage pick-up time.

condition_groups.label: noise and entertainment
condition_groups.note: This motion has no separate noise condition; the sound limit is the ban on amplified live entertainment, plus the 9 pm roof terrace closing in condition 20.

condition_groups.label: outdoor
condition_groups.note: The roof terrace is the only outdoor part of the restaurant that the conditions name.

condition_groups.label: alcohol
condition_groups.note: No condition of this motion is about alcohol.

featured_conditions.gloss: The roof terrace has to close by 9 pm, every day.
No amplified live entertainment at the restaurant.
Deliveries only between 8 am and 5 pm.
Before the first permit, file a plan for valet parking, staff parking and how diners get to the restaurant.
Six months after opening, the Commission holds a follow-up hearing, with a written report that includes any complaints recorded with the police and other feedback from neighbours.
Bins stay inside and out of sight, and garbage is not picked up before 6:30 am.
Name a community liaison for the neighbours and tell the Zoning Administrator who it is.
Some smell is expected; odour control equipment must stop anything stronger from escaping.

totals.note: "others" is every condition in the search except the one on screen (5,049 minus 1). Outside this motion there are 5,027 conditions in 351 motions.

open_questions: The local PostGIS copy was not running, on the first pass or at the fact-check of 2026-11-17. DataSF planning record facts (filing date 2017-02-23, close date 2017-07-19, the 2012 Certificate of Appropriateness case, the appeal record and the map point) were read both times from a local database snapshot of 2026-11-09 instead; the tables case_motions, case_conditions and record_labels were not consulted.
The dataset field "decided" for this record is 2017-07-19. That is the close date of the DataSF planning record; the motion itself was adopted on 2017-07-06. The story uses the motion date.

The DataSF planning record shows an appeal record opened 2017-08-10 and closed 2017-09-12 as "Closed - Appeal Denied", and notes that the performance period was "extended due to CEQA appeal and subsequent lawsuit". What exactly was appealed (the Conditional Use or the CEQA exemption), who appealed, which body decided it, and the outcome of the lawsuit are not in the records read here, so they are left out.
Whether the restaurant reopened, and when, is not in the motion or the planning record. The story should not say that it did or did not.

Six condition texts in conditions.json (numbers 7, 13, 15, 19, 20, 21) carry a scanning artefact: "T'he" or "'The" where the page prints "The". "text" is left exactly as in the dataset; "text_display" is the same text with only that artefact corrected. The lasting fix belongs in the dataset.
The motion has no condition about alcohol and no separate noise condition, so those two groups are empty or thin for this case.

In conditions.json the text of conditions 2, 6, 12 and 19 stops one sentence before the condition ends in the PDF (for example, condition 19 in the PDF goes on to say the liaison reports unresolved issues to the Zoning Administrator). The fact sheet keeps the dataset text; the glosses rely only on what the dataset text says.
The rear yard variance (2016-001273VAR) was decided by the Zoning Administrator, not in this motion. Its decision date is not in the motion and is left null.
Year-only timeline entries (1923, 1928, 2007) are given as a year because the motion gives no day or month.

The motion records that an expansion at the rear was built without a permit around 2007 (pp.1, 4) and that about 2 feet of it, extending into Pioneer Park, must be removed (p.9). The motion does not say who built it. If the story mentions it, it should keep the date and not attribute it to the present applicant.

The dataset text of each condition leaves out the closing line printed under it in the PDF ("For information about compliance, contact ..."). Together with the four cut-off conditions (2, 6, 12, 19), the story should not present the text as the complete printed condition without linking to the page.
Condition 12 contains a City program mailbox (the SFMTA bike parking address), copied from the dataset. It is an agency address, not a private person's.
